data.title: Revenge of the consumer: Walmart's $120 bundle takes on Amazon and Costco
data.description:
Walmart unveiled a bundled Walmart+ and Sam’s Club Plus membership option this week in a direct challenge to Amazon Prime and Costco . The joint membership costs $120 per year, which is a saving of $100 per year. It's also $19 cheaper than an annual Amazon Prime membership at $139 and $10 cheaper than Costco's $130 Executive membership but $55 more than Costco's $65 Gold Star membership. The biggest savings are for shoppers who now pay for both Prime and a Costco Executive membership, who would save $149 a year by switching to the bundle.

"This is a direct shot at Prime," United National Consumer Suppliers CEO Brett Rose told Retail Dive. He noted that at $120 per year a member gets a warehouse club, delivery, streaming, and gas thrown in. On paper, Walmart wins the value math easily, highlighted Rose.

“The timing tells you everything. Consumers are stretched heading into the holidays, and memberships lock in loyalty and recurring revenue before the spending gets decided,” Rose said. “Loyalty programs are what keep people coming back. However, not more so than lower prices.”

On Wall Street, Oppenheimer analyst Rupesh Parikh and his team believe consumers are the clear winners from the development due to the stronger combination of perks, the ability to have Walmart and Sam’s Club products delivered to your home with no markups, and minimal incremental costs to upgrade. "This new offering further strengthens Walmart's membership value proposition vs. Amazon Prime and COST. To the extent this membership program takes off, WMT should enjoy incremental wallet share gains, especially on the delivery front, but there is a likely initial P&L headwind near term," advised Parikh.

Looking ahead, the timing of the Walmart just ahead of the holidays could put incremental pressure on Amazon and Costco to dial up promotional activity.

data.title: Assam: Financial Inclusion Drive held in Kamrup, Loans distributed to rural beneficiaries
data.description:
Guwahati, Oct. 24 -- A major grassroots financial inclusion and credit outreach programme was held at the Malaybari Gaon Panchayat Auditorium near Khetri in Assam's Kamrup (Metro) district, focusing on rural financial security, women's empowerment and entrepreneurship.

The initiative was organised under the flagship Financial Inclusion Campaign led by the Department of Financial Services (DFS), Reserve Bank of India (RBI), State Bank of India (SBI) and National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD).

The campaign aimed to expand access to institutional credit and government-backed financial security schemes among rural households, with particular emphasis on strengthening women's economic self-reliance and promoting rural entrepreneurship, according to release.

The programme focused on increasing coverage under key financial inclusion schemes, including the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) and Atal Pension Yojana (APY).

Senior officials emphasised that financial inclusion must extend beyond opening bank accounts to enabling households to build financial resilience through savings, insurance coverage and accessible credit.

As part of the initiative, loan sanction letters and credit cheques were distributed among local beneficiaries and Self-Help Groups (SHGs), providing financial support to expand micro-enterprises, strengthen rural livelihoods and promote small businesses.

The event was attended by SBI Deputy General Manager Amit Ranjan, SBI Chief General Manager Atul Rathi, RBI Regional Director Sushmita Phukan, Lead District Manager Manoj Gogoi, NABARD Assistant General Manager Kirti Prabha and Malaybari Gaon Panchayat President Barnali Hazarika Das, among other officials and local representatives.

The outreach programme also highlighted the broader push towards financial inclusion and rural development in Assam since 2016. Initiatives such as Orunodoi, Self-Help Group credit linkage and doorstep financial services have contributed to expanding access to financial assistance and strengthening livelihood opportunities.

The programme underscored the role of institutional credit, financial literacy and women-led enterprises in promoting rural economic development, reducing financial vulnerability and advancing inclusive growth across the state.

data.title: "US objective is no more oil, nuclear issues, its total destruction of Iran": Foreign Affairs Expert Waiel Awwad
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- As crude oil prices surge to USD 117 per barrel and military tensions escalate across West Asia, Foreign Affairs Expert Waiel Awwad has warned that Washington's ultimate objective regarding Iran extends far beyond nuclear negotiations, aiming instead at complete regime change and regional dominance.

Speaking with ANI, Awwad asserted that conflicting rhetoric from the White House, ranging from threats to annihilate Iran to proposals for dialogue, reflects a deeper strategic shift aimed at reshaping the Middle East in tandem with Israel.

" It's a regime change, is the total destruction of Iran, disintegration of Iran, which makes Israel as a dominant force in the region," Awwad told ANI.

He added that the posture is also driven by domestic political pressure, stating, "This has also created some sort of a reassessment of the situation to improve his scoring in the American midterm election."

Addressing Tehran's retaliatory posture and reports of potential threats to cut Gulf undersea internet cables, the foreign affairs expert emphasised that for Tehran, the conflict has escalated into an "existential war."

"For Iran, it has been now an existential war, and for them, threatening that they will cause a global crisis is nothing but to make sure that if the United States goes this time for a war, Iran is prepared fully to defend itself and also to create more hurt to the United States," he noted.

He expressed scepticism regarding Washington's diplomatic willingness, pointing out that while Tehran had submitted proposals following the UN General Assembly, the US response remained non-committal.

"I don't believe that the United States is serious about the diplomatic outcome of this crisis," he remarked.

With crude oil hitting USD 117 per barrel, the highest level since April, Awwad highlighted the growing economic pressures on India's energy security, domestic inflation, and price stability.

Commenting on US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit to India and the visit to the strategic Reliance refinery in Jamnagar, Awwad pointed out that Washington is seeking to manoeuvre Venezuelan oil supplies into the global market to offset potential supply shocks.

"Jamnagar refinery is not merely a giant factory; in fact, it is one of India's strategic assets, where India can produce more diesel to serve the world and make some kind of balance in the international market," he stated.

He cautioned, however, that escalating conflict across maritime choke points like the Strait of Hormuz and Bab-el-Mandeb signals a broader geopolitical clash.

"It's a war of corridors and the war of dominance in the oil market," he said.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio visited Reliance Industries' Jamnagar facilities in Gujarat on Wednesday, home to the world's largest single-site refinery. US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor expressed his privilege at accompanying Rubio to Reliance's Jamnagar facilities.

In a post on X, Gor highlighted that India's imports of American liquefied petroleum gas had increased from below 10 per cent to 67 per cent over the preceding year, establishing the United States as India's primary LPG supplier.

Furthermore, he drew attention to Reliance's planned investment in constructing a new US oil refinery, characterising the initiative as a significant opportunity to expand American energy production and create jobs.

Earlier in the day, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed that Iran maintained full control over the Strait of Hormuz, asserting that security was being maintained for vessels operating in the region in accordance with Iranian regulations.

The claim came as the IRGC Navy alleged that two supertankers carrying a combined cargo of more than 4.5 million barrels of crude oil had struck naval mines while attempting to navigate what Tehran described as an unauthorised southern route through the strategic waterway.

Amid the escalating tensions, Iran warned that it would not allow US military vessels to enter the Persian Gulf, challenging Washington's assertions that Iranian military capabilities had been significantly weakened.

As per Iranian state broadcaster Press TV, Chief of the General Staff of Iran's Armed Forces, Major General Ali Abdollahi, said Iranian forces had rendered the US Navy ineffective in the region.

"The US president must only dream of their military and army entering the Persian Gulf again. They will take this wish to their graves," Abdollahi said. "We will under no circumstances and at no time allow US military vessels to enter the Persian Gulf," he added.

Abdollahi also questioned US President Donald Trump's repeated claims that Iran's nuclear facilities had been destroyed, asking why Washington continued to raise concerns about Tehran's nuclear programme if its facilities had already been eliminated.

"If you have destroyed everything, then what is the meaning of repeating this delusion?" Abdollahi said, alleging that such statements were intended to mislead public opinion.

The latest developments underscore the competing claims by Tehran and Washington over military capabilities, maritime security and the future of energy shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, amid continued uncertainty over the prospects for a diplomatic agreement.

data.title: India's basmati rice yield likely to be 5-10% higher this year: Industry leader
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- India's basmati rice yield is expected to increase by 5 to 10 per cent this year compared to the previous year, supported by favourable rainfall and better crop conditions, according to Rajeev Setia, President, Basmati IREF, and Joint Managing Director, Chaman Lal Setia Exports Ltd.

Speaking to ANI on the sidelines of the Bharat International Rice Conference 2026 in New Delhi, Setia said the monsoon and subsequent rainfall had supported the growth of the basmati crop, resulting in expectations of higher yields.

"The monsoon was reasonable... and thereafter there were good rains. Just look around, greenery we have all around. So in that way the crop grew and the yield in this particular year for basmati rice is higher," he said.

Asked about the expected increase, Setia said, "It will definitely be 5-10%... higher as compared to the preceding year."

The expected improvement in yields is significant for India's basmati rice industry, as higher agricultural productivity could support export availability amid expectations of growing international demand.

Setia also expressed optimism about the long-term demand for Indian basmati rice, pointing to the increasing popularity of Indian food across international markets.

"The requirement of Basmati is likely to grow in the time to come," he told ANI.

He said Indian basmati rice has established a presence across international markets, while his own company exports to 96 countries.

Setia noted that the growing popularity of Indian cuisine among consumers in Europe and the United States is helping expand the market for basmati rice beyond traditional consumers.

He also highlighted India's position in the global basmati rice trade, noting that the crop has geographical indication (GI) recognition and is cultivated in specific geographical regions.

India is one of the world's leading producers and exporters of basmati rice, with the crop playing an important role in the country's agricultural exports. Higher yields could improve supply availability, although actual export performance will also depend on international demand and market conditions.

The Bharat International Rice Conference 2026 is being held from October 23 to 25 in New Delhi, bringing together Indian exporters, international buyers and other stakeholders in the global rice trade.

data.title: Arthur Hayes Dumps $22 Million in Crypto, Warns of More Pain
data.description:
Arthur Hayes has sold about $22.28 million in crypto from Maelstrom’s directional book. Hayes, the family office’s chief investment officer, confirmed the exit on X and plans to sit out the market.

The post is a shift from his tone earlier this month. On October 15, Hayes urged traders to go long Bitcoin and Ethereum and trade an eventual bailout.

What Arthur Hayes Sold, and Why He Says He Left

Lookonchain data shows his biggest sale was 6,400 ETH, worth $15.2 million. Hayes also sold 14 million Ethena (ENA) for $2.76 million and 323,000 Uniswap for $2.24 million.

Smaller sales included 1.89 million Ether.fi (ETHFI) and stakes in Aerodrome Finance , Pendle (PENDLE), and Zama (ZAMA).

Hayes then confirmed the exit in a post, citing macro and geopolitical risks.

Did Hayes Sell at a Profit This Time?

Hayes says he took profits on ETH and ENA. Lookonchain valued his 6,400 ETH at $15.2 million, or about $2,375 per coin, though his cost for those coins is not public.

ENA offers a clearer comparison. In early August, he bought 9.05 million ENA for about $773,000, or roughly $0.085 per token.

Lookonchain valued Saturday’s ENA sale at about $0.20 per token. Still, it is unconfirmed whether the tokens sold are the same ones bought in August.

His newest bets fared worse. In mid-October, he bought Aerodrome, Pendle, and Zama tokens, Lookonchain reported.

He paid about $889,000 for them and sold them for about $856,000, based on Lookonchain’s prices at each trade. That leaves a loss of roughly $33,000.

The Slide Goes Beyond Hayes’ Tokens

His exit came during a broader market downturn. Six of the seven tokens he sold are down over the past month, according to BeInCrypto Markets.

The decline also puts Hayes’ earlier price targets in perspective. His September forecasts of $10,000 for ETH, $0.50 for ENA, and $2 for ETHFI remain well above current prices.

Broader market stress intensified this month. On October 15, crypto liquidations reached $942.1 million in 24 hours, with long positions accounting for 91.6% of the total.

On October 23, another selloff sent the Nasdaq down 2.6% and Bitcoin toward $81,400. Rising oil prices added to inflation concerns, putting monetary policy back in focus.

Why the Fed Is the Next Test

The Federal Reserve’s next decision, due October 28, could shape the outlook for risk assets. The Fed raised rates to 3.75%–4% on September 16, its first hike since July 2023. CME FedWatch data puts the odds of a hold at 90%.

The longer-term outlook remains uncertain. Minutes from September’s meeting showed most officials expected another hike by year-end. Hayes, by contrast, has argued that an eventual AI bailout would flood markets with new money.

His own trading history offers another reason to watch how he handles the latest exit. In August 2025, Hayes sold ETH near $3,507 and bought back nine days later at about $4,252.

A trader who copied the move would have paid roughly 21% more to reenter. For altcoin holders, the October 28 decision could help determine whether Hayes’ latest exit proves timely or premature.

data.title: Investors' recent money moves show a preference for lowering risks over boosting rewards
data.description:
By Philip van Doorn

Investors have been steadily pouring more money into 'quality' companies than 'momentum' stocks

The AI buildout is not the only thing investors cite as they move toward quality, according to Rene Reyna, Invesco's head of equity ETF strategy.

In a sign that investors are feeling anxious about the outlook for the stock market, they have recently shown a clear preference for "quality" shares, which tend to fare best during periods of broad market declines, over the previously highflying momentum stocks.

The S&P 500 is weighted by companies' market value, which means shares of companies with higher market capitalizations have more influence than those with lower market caps. There are various ways to invest along with the index or to try to outperform it by applying factors to hold subsets of the S&P 500.

If you hold shares of the $818 billion State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust SPY, an exchange-traded fund that tracks the S&P 500 SPX by holding all of its stocks, you can see how technology stalwarts and rapid growers dominate. The top five holdings of SPY - Nvidia (NVDA), Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN) and two common-share classes of Alphabet (GOOGL) (GOOG) - make up 30.6% of the portfolio.

There are various exchange-traded funds that include S&P 500 stocks but have different risk profiles, including the lower-risk $99 billion Invesco Equal Weight S&P 500 Index ETF RSP, in which each component is weighted the same, the even-lower-risk $19 billion Invesco S&P 500 Quality ETF SPHQ, and the more aggressive $22 billion Invesco S&P 500 Momentum ETF SPMO.

Rene Reyna, Invesco's head of equity ETF strategy, told MarketWatch that flows of new money into the quality ETF (SPHQ) have been steady for most of this year, with positive flows every month except for August. That month, $680 million flowed out of SPHQ, while $714 million flowed into the momentum ETF (SPMO). But in September, the action was subdued and in the opposite direction, with $3.4 million flowing into SPHQ and $43 million flowing out of SPMO. (See below for what constitutes quality and momentum.)

What might make the quality approach work, for now

During the first half of 2026, the equal-weighted approach fared well, with RSP returning 12%, while the S&P 500 returned 10.2%. But SPHQ did even better with a first-half return of 20.8%, while SPMO shined with a 36% return.

SPHQ holds the 100 stocks among the S&P 500 that rank highest according to a quality score that combines returns on equity, debt-to-book value and an "accruals ratio" of operating assets to total assets. The index tracked by this fund is rebalanced twice a year. Each stock is weighted by the product of its quality score and its market capitalization.

SPMO holds the 100 stocks of companies in the S&P 500 with the highest "momentum scores." Twice a year, the components of the S&P 500 are ranked by how much their prices have risen over the previous 12 months, then scored to take volatility into account. The portfolio is made up of the 20% of companies in the S&P 500 that score highest, which are then weighted by a combination of the momentum score and market capitalization

Here's the latest year-to-date performance chart for the three ETFs and the full S&P 500:

The Invesco S&P 500 Quality ETF has underperformed the S&P 500 so far this year. The Invesco Momentum ETF tends to outperform the full index during bull markets, but it can underperform during down periods for the broad market.

The chart shows that SPMO has experienced quite a bit of volatility this year, with prices coming down significantly since June 30.

Longer term, SPMO has been a stellar performer, with a five-year return of 137%, against 83% for the S&P 500 and 75% for SPHQ.

But according to Reyna, SPHQ is the safer play for investors during periods of souring sentiment. When asked how SPHQ might help investors who are questioning whether or not the trillions of dollars being spent on the build-out of artificial-intelligence infrastructure will eventually be justified through profits, he said that based on meetings with clients, "the challenge appears to be beyond AI."

He said that prior to the latest U.S. consumer-price index report, which showed inflation at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.7%, "we were looking at a low probability for another rate increase" when the Federal Reserve meets next week.

And Reyna said investors were also watching 10-year U.S. Treasury notes BX:TMUBMUSD10Y, which were yielding 5.02% early on Thursday. He said a 6% 10-year yield would represent a "challenge" to investors, who "might want to take a 6% return rather than the risk in the stock market."

When compared with the S&P 500's price movement, SPMO has had 142.48% upside capture over the past year, with 106.4% downside capture, according to Reyna. Meanwhile, SPHQ has had 86.05% upside capture, with only 61.1% downside capture. Basically, you might not make as much with quality relative to momentum when the market is rising, but you also lose a lot less when the market falls.

For investors who wish to stay invested while softening the effect of a possible market correction, the lower-volatility approach has been gaining in popularity.

-Philip van Doorn

data.title: Train hits minibus in Russia's Far East, killing six
data.description:
Six people were killed and one person was injured when a train collided with a minibus in Russia's Far Eastern Jewish Autonomous Region, local railway authorities said.

According to railway officials, the minibus attempted to cross the tracks at a level crossing despite a red signal and was struck by a passenger train bound for the city of Blagoveshchensk.

All the victims were in the minibus. The train's passengers and crew were not hurt.

The state-run RIA news agency, citing regional prosecutors, reported that all the minibus occupants were foreign nationals, but did not specify their nationalities.

data.title: Indonesia cuts pipeline gas exports to Singapore by about 9%
data.description:
Indonesia cut 31 million standard cubic feet of gas per day (mmscfd) from its pipeline natural gas exports to Singapore starting on Saturday to divert supply to the domestic power sector, upstream oil and gas regulator SKK Migas said.

  • Indonesia cut 15 mmscfd from its supply to Singapore from Natuna and another 16 mmscfd of gas from Sumatra, SKK Migas chairman Djoko Siswanto told Reuters on Saturday.

  • Singapore's Energy Market Authority said the total reduction amounts to 17 bbtud over a period of 18 days, which is "less than 2% of our total daily gas demand of more than 1,000 bbtud".

  • "EMA understands that our importers will pursue all relevant recourse in their contracts for the gas supply disruption," the Energy Market Authority spokesperson said

  • Singapore's Energy Market Authority said state gas buyer GasCo is ready to import more LNG at any time and that the country has sufficient energy supplies for national demand

  • Most of Indonesia’s gas exports to Singapore are delivered via pipeline, and the cuts would account for around 9% of that supply

  • “In order to safeguard the reliability of domestic gas supplies for electricity generation, effective today, gas supplies previously destined for Singapore are being redirected for domestic use,” said Djoko

  • The gas is being redirected to meet electricity needs in Batam, Bintan and Sumatra, he said

  • Batam and several cities in Indonesia's Riau Islands province suffered a blackout that lasted 16 hours earlier this month

  • Indonesia energy minister Bahlil Lahadalia earlier this week said he would prioritise natural resources use for domestic needs, and review contracts to maintain energy security

data.title: Lumax Auto Q2 results: Profit jumps 58%; new Manesar plant targets ₹500 crore turnover
data.description:
Lumax Auto Technologies reported a strong performance in the second quarter of FY27, with net profit rising 57.5% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹105.5 crore, compared with ₹67 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

The company' s revenue increased 34.5% YoY to ₹1,555.5 crore from ₹1,156.4 crore a year earlier. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rose 32.4% to ₹204.7 crore from ₹154.6 crore in the year-ago quarter.

However, EBITDA margin edged down to 13.2% from 13.4% in the corresponding period last year.

Lumax Auto plans ₹150 crore mechatronics plant in Manesar

Separately, Lumax Auto Technologies plans to set up a new mechatronics manufacturing facility in Manesar, Haryana, with a capital outlay of around ₹150 crore.

The facility will manufacture electronic components, including body control modules, for leading original equipment manufacturers (OEMs). The investment will be funded through a combination of debt and internal accruals, stated the exchange filing.

The project is expected to be commissioned in two phases, beginning in the third quarter of FY28. Once operational at peak capacity, the facility is expected to generate annualised turnover of around ₹500 crore.

Lumax Japp Allied Technologies ceases to be subsidiary

The company also disclosed that the sale of its entire 50% equity stake in Lumax Japp Allied Technologies Private to Germany-based Japp Holding GmbH was completed during the current period.

The board had approved the sale on May 8, 2026. Following the completion of the transaction, Lumax Japp Allied Technologies ceased to be a subsidiary of Lumax Auto Technologies.

The company had recognised an impairment loss of ₹7.04 crore as an exceptional item in its standalone financial results for the year ended March 31, 2026, in connection with the proposed transaction.

Anmol Jain, managing director of Lumax Auto Technologies, said the company delivered another strong quarter despite a challenging operating environment, with revenue growth outpacing the broader industry and profitability improving on the back of broad-based demand across product categories.

For the first half of FY27, revenue grew 34% year-on-year, while profit after tax before minority interest increased 64%, Jain said. He attributed the performance to the scale-up of existing products and deeper penetration of the company's value-added product portfolio.

Jain noted that automotive production continued to grow across vehicle segments in the September quarter, supported by improved affordability following the implementation of GST 2.0. However, rising input costs, including crude-linked polymer prices, higher costs and lead times for electronic components, freight expenses and rupee depreciation, remain key factors to watch.

Shares of Lumax Auto Technologies ended 0.53% lower at ₹1,807.70 on the NSE on Friday, October 23. The stock has declined 11.1% over the past month but remains up 12.5% so far this year.

data.title: CoinShares BTF Liquidation Sets Cash Payout And Earlier Options Expiry
data.description:
TL;DR: CoinShares’ Bitcoin and Ether ETF has reached cash settlement. An OCC notice confirms the payout and brings later-dated BTF options forward to a November 20 expiry.

The closing chapter for CoinShares’ Bitcoin and Ether ETF now comes with a precise cash amount and a deadline for outstanding options. The details matter because a fund can stop trading before every contract linked to it has expired.

According to an October 22 notice from the Options Clearing Corporation, liquidation proceeds were distributed at $22.16255605 per BTF share. The adjusted deliverable for a standard options contract is $2,216.26 in cash, replacing its former share-based exposure.

The BTF option symbol remains unchanged. That continuity should not be mistaken for continuity in the investment underneath it: the contract now references a defined cash deliverable rather than an operating crypto fund.

November 20 Becomes The Final Date For Later Series

OCC says series previously expiring after November 20, 2026 will expire on that date instead. Contracts with earlier expirations retain those dates. Existing American-style options remain exercisable before expiry, and exercised contracts continue to settle in one business day.

Settlement is based on the difference between the contract’s total strike amount and its cash deliverable. The adjustment ends the delayed-settlement treatment that applied on October 21.

Those mechanics are separate from a directional view on Bitcoin or Ethereum. Once the deliverable has become cash, subsequent coin-price moves do not recreate the ETF exposure that shareholders previously held.

A Futures Fund Reaches The End Of Its Run

CoinShares announced the closure in September, alongside its Altcoins ETF, DIME. October 20 was the final day for share trading and creation or redemption orders, with liquidation planned around October 21.

The manager said remaining holders would receive cash based on net asset value after provision for the fund’s expenses and liabilities. Its board approved the wind-down following the investment adviser’s recommendation.

BTF’s structure is also relevant. The fund’s own product information describes a portfolio built primarily around Bitcoin and Ether futures, with cash and high-quality debt supporting the strategy. It was not a vehicle that simply kept an equivalent number of coins in custody for every share.

Its published figures as of October 20 showed approximately $15.96 million in assets. That is a dated snapshot of this individual product, not evidence of money leaving every fund managed by CoinShares.

For the wider crypto exchange ecosystem, closures are a reminder that investment wrappers carry their own lifecycles. Fund shares, direct coin holdings and derivatives can respond differently to the same corporate event.

The new information here is the completed payout and the revised options timetable. Treating it as a fresh Bitcoin sale announcement would miss what has actually changed: BTF’s remaining obligations are being resolved in cash.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: Trump says he may move White House press corps
data.description:
By Jason Lange

US President Donald Trump confirmed on Saturday he may move the White House press corps to a different location.

In a social media post, Trump dismissed a report that he planned to remove the White House press room and restore a historic swimming pool on the site, saying he had never "even thought to do such a stupid thing."

But he said he could relocate the press corps from its current position in the White House.

"I may move the Fake News to a less obnoxious location," Trump said in the post.

The New York Times reported on Tuesday that Trump had urged then-press secretary Karoline Leavitt in August to move news conferences out of the White House's James S. Brady Press Briefing Room, although the idea was never implemented.

According to the report, the president told aides he would rather have an indoor therapy pool that was installed at the site during Franklin D. Roosevelt's administration. The Nixon administration replaced the pool with the press briefing room.

Trump has regularly accused US media of unfair reporting about his administration.

Last month, Trump briefly banned journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico from White House grounds and said other outlets could face similar restrictions. Free speech advocates have said the move violated First Amendment protections for a free press.

The White House reinstated their access after an order from a federal judge who deemed the ban likely unconstitutional, although the Trump administration is still contesting the case.

data.title: Parabilis Medicines Presents Updated Phase 1/2 Data for Zolucatetide Demonstrating Compelling Efficacy and Favorable Safety and Tolerability Profile in Patients with Desmoid Tumors
data.description:
Key points:
  • Objective response rate of 72.2% among response-evaluable patients receiving a starting dose of ≥450 mg at 32-week landmark
  • Disease control rate of 100% across all response-evaluable patients receiving a starting dose of ≥450 mg, with no disease progression and no treatment discontinuations due to TRAEs
  • Data informed FDA-aligned dose and regimen selection for upcoming PEDESTAL Phase 3 registrational trial, with initiation planned in the first half of 2027 and topline results anticipated in 2029
  • Company to host investor webcast on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at 18:00 CEST (12:00 p.m. EDT)

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., Oct. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Parabilis Medicines , a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company dedicated to creating extraordinary medicines for patients with serious diseases by unlocking historically undruggable targets, today announced updated safety and efficacy data for zolucatetide, the first and only direct inhibitor of the β-catenin:TCF interaction, in patients with desmoid tumors. The data were presented today in an oral presentation at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026, taking place October 23–27, 2026, in Madrid, Spain.

The updated results, based on a June 22, 2026, data cutoff, include data from both the dose escalation and dose optimization portions of the ongoing Phase 1/2 trial and reinforce the strong efficacy and favorable safety and tolerability profile observed with zolucatetide. Among response-evaluable patients who began treatment at a starting dose of ≥450 mg, zolucatetide demonstrated an objective response rate (ORR) of 72.2% (13/18) in a 32-week landmark analysis. A disease control rate (DCR) of 100% was observed across all 46 response-evaluable patients who received a starting dose of ≥450 mg, with no disease progression.

Data from a three-arm randomized dose optimization trial supported selection of a 450 mg weekly induction regimen administered for four cycles, followed by 300 mg every two weeks for long-term maintenance. Following productive end-of-Phase 2 discussions, Parabilis has reached alignment with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on the selected dose and regimen, on the use of a placebo-controlled study design, and on progression-free survival (PFS) as the primary endpoint for registrational development.

Parabilis plans to initiate the randomized, double-blind PEDESTAL Phase 3 trial (Phase 3 Evaluation of DESmoid Tumor Activity with zoLucatetide) in the first half of 2027, with topline results anticipated in 2029.

“Desmoid tumors are chronic and life-altering for patients, often affecting people at a young age, and patients need treatments that can deliver rapid, deep and durable tumor responses with a tolerability profile suited for long-term treatment,” said Mathai Mammen, M.D., Ph.D., Chairman, CEO and President of Parabilis Medicines. “We designed zolucatetide to directly inhibit β-catenin:TCF, a historically undruggable target at the heart of the biology driving these tumors. The depth and consistency of responses we are seeing, together with the favorable safety and tolerability profile observed to date, reinforce our conviction that zolucatetide has the potential to deliver a truly differentiated medicine and meaningfully expand the number of patients who can benefit from treatment. We are very pleased with the clarity of the FDA’s feedback on our registrational development strategy, and with our Phase 3 regimen selected, we are moving with urgency to bring this medicine to patients.”

Updated Phase 1/2 Results

As of the June 22, 2026, data cutoff, 76 patients with desmoid tumors had been enrolled and treated across all dose levels in the dose escalation and dose optimization portions of the trial. Median age was 37 years (range 19–80), and 69.7% of patients were female. The population included both patients who had previously been treated with and failed gamma-secretase inhibitors (GSIs) and patients naive to GSIs.

A total of 48 patients began treatment at a starting induction dose of ≥450 mg, prior to down-dosing for maintenance. Two patients were started at 900 mg, but had an average dose of 400–500 mg over the first four months of treatment. Of these 48 patients, 46 were response-evaluable, and 18 had scans at 32 weeks. Median time on treatment for this cohort was 4.7 months (range 0.5–22.3), reflecting recent enrollment of a substantial portion of the cohort.

Efficacy

  • ORR per RECIST 1.1 was 72.2% (13/18) among all patients evaluable at the 32-week landmark
  • A disease control rate (DCR) of 100% was observed across all 46 response-evaluable patients
  • Responses were observed irrespective of prior gamma-secretase inhibitor (GSI) exposure or CTNNB1 or APC mutation status
  • No evidence of disease progression or resistance

Safety

  • Zolucatetide continued to demonstrate a favorable safety and tolerability profile at the selected doses for Phase 3 registrational development
  • Treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were predominantly low-grade; the most commonly reported TRAEs were fatigue, alopecia and nausea
  • No patients discontinued treatment due to TRAEs
  • Not associated with ovarian toxicity or high-grade gastrointestinal or skin toxicities commonly reported with GSIs

“The early clinical results with zolucatetide are encouraging, particularly the magnitude and apparent rapidity of tumor responses observed to date,” said Mrinal Gounder, M.D., Sarcoma Medical Oncologist and Early Drug Development Specialist at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, and presenting author of the study. “Desmoid tumors can impose a substantial physical and emotional burden on patients, and therapies capable of achieving meaningful tumor shrinkage while maintaining acceptable tolerability remain an important clinical goal. These findings support further investigation of zolucatetide in the planned Phase 3 trial.”

The Phase 1/2 trial is ongoing in patients with desmoid tumors and a range of other tumor types driven by alterations in the Wnt/β-catenin pathway, and follow-up is continuing. Zolucatetide has received Fast Track and Orphan Drug Designations from the FDA for the treatment of desmoid tumors.

These findings provide further clinical validation of the potential of the Company's Helicon™ platform to unlock disease-driving targets historically considered undruggable.

Investor Webcast

Parabilis will host an investor webcast on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at 18:00 CEST (12:00 p.m. EDT) to discuss the updated zolucatetide data that will be presented at ESMO Congress 2026. The webcast will be available on the Investors section of the Parabilis website at https://investors.parabilismed.com. Both the presentation and a replay of the webcast will be available following the event.

About Desmoid Tumors

Desmoid tumors are locally invasive soft-tissue tumors that arise in connective tissues and can be aggressive and recurrent, often causing chronic pain, limited mobility, disfigurement and organ dysfunction. An estimated 30,000 people in the U.S. alone are living with desmoid tumors, including approximately 11,000 who are actively managed, with significant unmet need globally as well. Desmoid tumors typically present in young adults, predominantly females, with many patients requiring prolonged or intermittent treatment. Wnt/β-catenin pathway-activating mutations are the causal driver of desmoid tumors, yet no approved therapies directly target this underlying biology of the disease.

About Zolucatetide

Zolucatetide is an investigational first-in-class and first and only direct inhibitor of the interaction between β-catenin and the T-cell factor (TCF) family of transcription factors, a genetically validated driver of numerous cancers and other serious diseases that has long been considered undruggable. Developed using Parabilis’ Helicon™ peptide platform, zolucatetide is designed to prevent the activation of disease-driving genes by directly targeting β-catenin:TCF, a key downstream node in the Wnt/β-catenin pathway. This approach has the potential to address aberrant Wnt/β-catenin signaling regardless of the upstream APC or β-catenin mutations driving pathway activation, potentially overcoming a key limitation of approaches targeting earlier steps in the pathway.

Zolucatetide is currently being evaluated in an ongoing Phase 1/2 clinical trial (NCT05919264) across a range of indications, including desmoid tumors, familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP), adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma (ACP), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and additional Wnt-driven tumor types.

About Parabilis Medicines

Parabilis Medicines is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company dedicated to creating extraordinary medicines for patients with serious diseases by unlocking biologically important targets long considered undruggable. The Company has pioneered a new class of alpha-helical peptides – Helicons™ – capable of modulating intracellular proteins that have historically been beyond the reach of conventional medicines. The Company's lead investigational medicine, zolucatetide, is the first and only direct inhibitor of the β-catenin:TCF interaction, a central node in the Wnt/β-catenin pathway that has eluded drug developers for decades. Zolucatetide is being evaluated in the clinic across multiple Wnt/β-catenin-driven diseases, including desmoid tumors, familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP), adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma (ACP), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and a range of other rare and common solid tumor indications. Beyond zolucatetide, Parabilis is pursuing a follow-on β-catenin degrader program and advancing additional Helicon-based programs focused on other challenging targets, including ERG and allosteric ARON in prostate cancer, where we believe our medicines could have life-altering impact. data.title: Kotak Mahindra Bank Q2 Profit Rises 29%; Net Interest Margin Falls To 4.31%
data.description:
Higher interest income and lower provisions drive earnings growth, while FCNR(B) deposit mobilisation weighs on margins despite strong loan and deposit growth

Kotak Mahindra Bank reported a 29 per cent year-on-year rise in standalone net profit to Rs 4,212 crore for the September quarter of FY27, supported by higher interest income and lower provisions. However, its net interest margin (NIM) declined to 4.31 per cent as the bank mobilised foreign currency deposits during the quarter.

The lender’s standalone profit rose from Rs 3,253 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Consolidated net profit increased 26 per cent to Rs 5,645 crore from Rs 4,468 crore a year earlier, according to its results announced on 24 October.

Net interest income (NII), the difference between interest earned and interest paid, grew 16 per cent year-on-year to Rs 8,459 crore from Rs 7,311 crore. Sequentially, NII increased 7 per cent from Rs 7,928 crore in the June quarter.

The bank’s NIM, which measures the income earned from interest-bearing assets relative to their cost, fell from 4.54 per cent a year earlier and 4.53 per cent in the preceding quarter. Kotak attributed the moderation largely to the mobilisation of foreign currency non-resident (bank), or FCNR(B), deposits.

The bank raised around Rs 55,344 crore through FCNR(B) deposits during the quarter and extended loans of approximately Rs 16,110 crore through its international branches.

Asset Quality Improves

Provisions declined 15 per cent year-on-year to Rs 803 crore from Rs 947 crore, supporting profitability. Annualised credit cost fell to 0.35 per cent from 0.79 per cent in the year-ago quarter.

Asset quality also improved. Gross non-performing assets (GNPA) declined to 1.04 per cent of advances as of 30 September 2026, compared with 1.39 per cent a year earlier. Net non-performing assets fell to 0.24 per cent from 0.32 per cent.

The bank’s net advances grew 25 per cent year-on-year to Rs 5.77 lakh crore, while total deposits rose 23 per cent to Rs 6.51 lakh crore. Excluding FCNR(B) deposits, deposit growth stood at 13 per cent.

The current account and savings account (CASA) ratio declined to 38.2 per cent from 42.3 per cent a year earlier. Excluding FCNR(B) deposits, the ratio stood at 41.8 per cent.

data.title: Bitcoin ETFs See $635M Outflow In A Day As BTC Slips Back To September Levels
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bitcoin slid back toward $80,000 on Saturday, more than a month after it last broke that level.
  • U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs lost over $635 million on Thursday, and $137.94 million on Friday, according to SoSoValue data.
  • Galaxy's Alex Thorn said he is "very confident" the industry will swing back toward decentralized crypto.

Bitcoin’s (BTC) price dropped to around $80,000 on Saturday, a level it last traded at in September, as U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds lost over $635 million on Thursday.

The slide came as investors turned sellers on US spot Bitcoin ETFs, with the funds seeing over $635 million in net outflows on Thursday, according to SoSoValue data. This nearly matched the $681 million the funds lost over the entire week ending October 9.

SoSoValue data also showed it was nearly three times last week's $229 million in outflows.

Bitcoin’s price traded around $80,500, down over 1% over 24 hours, at the time of writing. The drop took the price back to a level it last broke last month, when it traded around the $80,000 range on 18th September.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter stayed at ‘low’ levels over the past day.

Oil Adds To The Pressure

Bitcoin's slide also came as oil prices climbed higher. Brent crude rose over 3% on Friday to settle at $116.72 a barrel, its highest settlement since April, as high oil prices stoked inflation fears on Wall Street.

Reports that the U.S. and Israel could be preparing fresh strikes on Iran had revived geopolitical worries. Market participants still priced in a 90% chance that the Federal Reserve would hold rates steady of 375-400 basis points at its meeting next week, according to the CME FedWatch tool, while 10% priced a rate hike of 400 to 425 basis points for the upcoming Oct 27 to 28 Federal Reserve meeting.

Meanwhile, CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost said that oil does not move Bitcoin directly. https://x.com/cryptoquant_com/status/2113538742119977146?s=20

According to him, the bigger headwind was the tougher economy that expensive oil created. He noted that Bitcoin's momentum had historically cooled when Brent trended strongly above its yearly average.

Thorn Sees ‘Pendulum’ Swinging Back

Speaking on Galaxy's "Galaxy Brains" podcast, Thorn took a longer view. He described crypto as moving between "the suits," the banks and brokerages that embraced blockchain technology but kept Bitcoin at arm's length, and "the cypherpunks," who backed decentralized money.

He explained that the suits had the upper hand right now, but that has also happened before. Around 2015 and 2016, banks championed "blockchain not Bitcoin" and built private networks, but "ultimately none of those really worked." Thorn said the industry had since swung back. "I've seen it happen, you know, four or five times now, this pendulum swing," he said. "And I'm very confident it will happen again."

He urged Bitcoin holders to "not despair," adding that "Bitcoin is here to stay." While "we can't know for certain," Thorn said it looked "pretty certain" that the $58,000 range Bitcoin touched in June marked the bottom of this cycle.

October has historically been Bitcoin's best month. However, Thorn noted that "we haven't had uh back-to-back uh red Octobers since 2011 and 2012."

Bitcoin, the apex cryptocurrency, was down over 8% year-to-date (YTD).

  • $50M Treasury Reserve Cushion: Establishes a safety buffer for sustainable ecosystem operations.
  • Expanded Funding Sources: Integrates GasFree revenue alongside JustLend and USDD to cover 100% of JUST core products.
  • ~$20.34M Capital Injection: Unlocks legacy surplus funds to be released in phases for future buybacks.
  • JUST DAO Execution: Complete on-chain execution with full transparency and open-source verification.

Following its recent brand refresh on October 23, JUST—the flagship on-chain DeFi infrastructure on TRON—officially unveiled its upgraded JST Buyback & Burn initiative that strengthens the value-accrual framework of the native governance token. Building on previous funding sources from JustLend and USDD, the upgraded mechanism incorporates business revenue from GasFree while allocating $20.34 million in capital surplus to future token repurchases. These changes diversify the protocol’s revenue base and set a structured process for deploying surplus capital.

The updated framework expands JST buyback funding from a dual-revenue stream (i.e., JustLend and USDD) to a more robust three-pillar model (i.e., JustLend, USDD, and GasFree), reinforced by phased injections of existing funds. Beyond simply adding capital, this upgrade ensures that growth in each JUST product line directly accrues to JST’s underlying value. It underscores JUST’s long-term commitment to token value accrual while tightly aligning protocol incentives with JST holders and the broader community.

JST Buyback & Burn Upgraded: $50M Safety Cushion, GasFree Revenue Integration, and $20.34M Surplus Injection

As the native governance token of the JUST ecosystem, JST’s underlying value support and utility mechanisms have always been a central focus for the community. With the successful completion of the 5th buyback and burn on October 16, Phase 1 of the JST Buyback and Burn program concluded smoothly, paving the way for the upgraded mechanism alongside JUST’s broader brand refresh.

According to the Announcement: Upgrade to the JST Buyback & Burn Mechanism, the newly updated framework outlines key structural arrangements across five core areas, establishing clear risk boundaries while securing a more stable and predictable capital foundation for future buybacks:

  • $50M Treasury Safety Floor: A baseline reserve of at least $50 million will be maintained long-term to manage risk scenarios, guarantee liquidity, and ensure protocol solvency under extreme market conditions.
  • More Diversified Funding Sources: The upgraded model integrates GasFree revenue alongside existing JustLend and USDD streams, extending buyback capital across all three core JUST product lines. Specific sources now include revenue from JustLend’s sTRX staking and SBM, GasFree income, and the USDD protocol revenue exceeding the $10 million threshold.
  • Structured Surplus Capital Deployment: All protocol funds above the $50 million treasury reserve floor are dedicated entirely to JST buybacks. An initial $20.34 million—sourced from cumulative GasFree earnings and surplus treasury reserves above the safety floor—has been unlocked, and will be deployed across four buyback rounds starting in Q4 2026.
  • Buyback & Burn Execution: The protocol is adopting a “continuous buyback, periodic burn” approach. Funded by 100% of revenue across all product lines, open-market buybacks will adjust dynamically to prevailing market depth and liquidity, with accumulated tokens burned on a regular schedule.
  • On-Chain Governance: All buybacks and burns will be executed by JUST DAO. Key financial figures will be disclosed to the community on a regular basis, and every transaction will remain fully verifiable on-chain. 

Compared to Phase 1, this upgrade introduces three structural shifts:

  • Clearer capital boundaries. The $50 million reserve floor creates a solvency backstop while defining the boundaries of capital eligible for buybacks. 
  • More diversified funding sources. Rather than relying primarily on JustLend and USDD, integrating GasFree extends revenue capture across the entire JUST ecosystem. Meanwhile, deploying roughly $20.34 million in surplus funds across future tranches smooths buyback execution and ensures an orderly transition between mechanism phases. 
  • Streamlined execution under unified governance. By adopting a “continuous buyback, periodic burn” strategy, the consolidated JUST DAO (formerly JustLend DAO) takes full operational ownership of buybacks and burns. This aligns governance and execution under a single authority, matching JUST’s brand consolidation and holistic governance roadmap. 

In essence, the updated mechanism follows a clear tripartite playbook: secure the downside, deploy surplus capital, and compound with organic growth. It first anchors ecosystem stability with the $50 million reserve floor, primes buyback momentum by releasing roughly $20.34 million in surplus funds, and then hands the baton to ongoing revenues from all three verticals—turning JST buybacks into a sustainable, business-backed deflationary engine.

GasFree Poised to Become the Second Growth Engine for JST Buybacks After JustLend

The integration of GasFree revenue represents the key highlight of this mechanism upgrade. Scheduled to begin capital allocations in Q4 2026, GasFree has demonstrated strong cash-flow generation and is positioned to become the second growth engine for JST buyback funding after JustLend.

Built on TRON, GasFree is a native gasless solution that lets users pay transaction fees directly with the tokens they transfer, removing the friction of holding TRX or other native tokens just to move funds. By enabling single-asset fee settlement, GasFree eliminates one of the most stubborn usability hurdles in on-chain transfers. The service currently supports gasless transfers for both USDT and USDD.

Operationally, GasFree’s user base and network activity continue to climb at a rapid pace. As of October 23, GasFree has processed over $157.1 billion in cumulative stablecoin transfer volume across more than 9.14 million transactions, serving an aggregate user base exceeding 500,000 unique addresses. This surging operational momentum provides the solid backing for GasFree to consistently fuel the buyback pool and establish itself as JST’s second major growth engine.

From a revenue standpoint, GasFree’s profitability is backed by hard data. It has proven to be a vital growth engine since its March 2025 rollout, generating approximately $12.03 million in cumulative revenue through Q3 2026. This performance underpinned the recent extraction of roughly $20.34 million in surplus funds, sourced directly from GasFree’s accrued earnings and surplus treasury holdings above the reserve floor.

As GasFree’s financial contribution accelerates, JST’s buyback-and-burn model enters a new stage of multi-business synergy. The token’s value-accrual mechanism is now deeply tied to the growth of the broader JUST ecosystem and fully synchronized with the protocol’s multi-product expansion.

Diversified Value Accrual: JUST’s Core Products Unite to Back JST

Under the updated mechanism, GasFree revenue is now directly allocated to JST buybacks, alongside qualifying net revenue from USDD. This marks a pivotal evolution: JST burns no longer rely solely on JustLend. Instead, they are fueled by a diversified, multi-product revenue base spanning JustLend, USDD, and GasFree.

This multi-pronged funding approach mirrors the broader JUST rebrand. Moving forward, JustLend, USDD, and GasFree unite under a single brand and user gateway—with JUST DAO steering cross-product governance, ecosystem synergy, and sustainable tokenomics for JST.

JST serves as the native governance token for the entire JUST ecosystem. Through this unified rebrand and the rollout of JUST DAO governance, JST’s value foundation now spans the protocol’s core utility layers: lending and resource markets via JustLend, decentralized stablecoin infrastructure via USDD, and gasless transfer settlement via GasFree. JST is no longer anchored to a single product line; its value capture is directly tied to the growth of the entire ecosystem.

As a pillar of TRON’s financial infrastructure, JUST commands roughly $12.2 billion in Total Value Locked (TVL)—consistently securing nearly half of the network’s total liquidity, with all three business pillars holding leading positions in their respective verticals.

Among them, JustLend remains foundational: having fully funded the initial phase of JST buybacks and burns, it now provides the core yield baseline under the upgraded mechanism. As of October 23, JustLend’s TVL surpassed $7.13 billion, with its supply-borrow market (SBM) driving approximately $3.71 billion, cementing its status as a global DeFi lending leader. In the staking sector, total TRX staked has crossed 9.83 billion. At the same time, through sTRX-powered Energy solutions, JustLend has become a primary Energy gateway for the TRON network, scaling both on-demand Energy purchases and long-term rental services.

Meanwhile, GasFree continues to scale as a key revenue driver. In late September, GasFree partnered with Binance Web3 Wallet to introduce TRC-20 USDT gas fee delegation. Users can now pay network fees directly in USDT without needing to hold TRX. Securing integration with a Tier-1 wallet validates GasFree’s business model and significantly expands its addressable market and fee-generation capacity.

data.title: EPS-95 pension: Bombay High Court rules in favour of private sector employees seeking pension on higher wages
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- Private sector employees seeking a higher pension under the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS), 1995, have received relief from the Bombay High Court.

The court has ruled that the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) cannot reject an employee's application for a higher pension merely because the employer's provident fund (PF) trust rules cap contributions at the statutory wage ceiling or do not expressly allow higher pension contributions.

In its October 19, 2026, judgment, Justice Sandeep V. Marne set aside EPFO orders rejecting applications filed by over 40 private-sector employees of establishments including Abbott India, Tata Communications, Raymond Steel and BEST Undertaking.

The court directed EPFO to process and allow the petitioners' joint-option applications within eight weeks.

Employees and employers make contributions towards the employee's provident fund, while a portion of the employer's contribution is ordinarily diverted to the EPS, subject to the scheme's rules.

The statutory wage ceiling is the salary limit used to calculate contributions under the applicable rules. The EPS ceiling was raised to Rs.15,000 a month in 2014 (further raised to Rs.25,000 from 17 September 2026).

However, eligible employees who had contributed to their PF on actual salaries above the statutory ceiling can seek a higher pension by opting to calculate pension contributions on higher wages, subject to the scheme's conditions.

This is where the joint option comes in. It is an option exercised jointly by the employee and employer to seek pension based on higher wages instead of being restricted to the statutory ceiling.

"The common issue of law which is involved in these Petitions is whether private trust rules of a provident fund trust of an exempted establishment under the Employees' Provided Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 (EPF Act) can govern the contribution to the Employees' Pension Fund of employers or restrict the exercise of Joint Option under paragraph 11(3) /11 (4) of Employees Pension Scheme,1995 (EPS, 1995)," according to the ruling document.

For example, if an employee's salary was Rs.40,000 a month and PF contributions were made on that actual salary, the employee may seek a higher pension based on higher wages, subject to eligibility and the required contributions.

Some employers had their own PF trusts because their establishments were exempted from the usual EPF arrangement. The trusts' internal rules restricted contributions to the statutory wage ceiling or did not expressly provide for higher pension contributions.

EPFO relied on these rules to reject the employees' joint-option applications. In some cases, it also cited missing documents or questions about contributions on eligible salary components.

The employees challenged these decisions, arguing that internal PF trust rules could not override the statutory EPS provisions.

Justice Sandeep V. Marne noted that "I have heard Mr. Surana, the learned counsel appearing for the Petitioners, who submits that the issue is conclusively answered by the judgment of the Apex Court in Sunil Kumar B. (supra), which holds that an exempted and unexempted establishments stand on par."

"He submits that the Trust Rules operate only in the field of provident fund and that the same has no bearing on employee's entitlement for pension on higher wages."

"Per contra, Ms. Gandhi, the learned counsel appearing for the Respondent-EPFO submits that the Applications of the Petitioners are rightly rejected by the Competent Authority after duly applying its mind to the entire material on record," Marne added.

Several High Courts had ruled that PF trust rules could not, by themselves, be used to deny eligible employees the benefit of a higher pension under the EPS. The Bombay High Court held that the rules governing an employer's PF trust could not be used as the sole ground to reject an otherwise eligible employee's joint option.

Marne said, "In my view, therefore all the Petitions deserve to be allowed. As consistently held by various High Courts, the rules/deeds of provident fund trusts of an exempted establishment operate only in respect of the provident fund, unless an exemption under Section 17(1)(c) of the EPF Act read with paragraph 39 of the EPS, 1995, including joint option, applies to the employees in same manner as the employees of unexempted establishments."

"A joint option cannot be rejected on the ground that the Trust Rules either envisage a cap /ceiling or employer's contribution or that Trust Rules did not provide for joint option on higher pension on the ground that employer did not remit pension contribution on the wages exceeding the ceiling," he added.

The court also addressed cases where employers could not produce old records. Referring to earlier judgments, it noted that alternative verification methods, including giving employees an opportunity to be heard, should be considered where records are unavailable.

The EPFO had also argued that contributions on certain salary components needed verification. However, the court found no reason to distinguish the Tata Communications case on the grounds presented, as the central reason for rejection remained the restrictions in the trust rules.

The court set aside the EPFO orders rejecting the applications and directed the authorities to process and allow the petitioners' joint options for higher pension within eight weeks. The petitions were allowed, with no order as to costs.

"Impugned orders passed by the EPFO rejecting applications filed by the Petitioners for availing benefit of pension on higher wages under paragraph 11(3) /11(4) of the Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995 are set aside," according to the ruling.

The court considered the Supreme Court's ruling in EPFO v. Sunil Kumar B., which upheld the 2014 EPS amendments. The Supreme Court had also held that employees who contributed to the PF on actual wages exceeding the statutory ceiling could not be debarred from exercising the higher-pension option solely on that ground, subject to the scheme's conditions.

No. The judgment does not automatically entitle every EPFO member to a higher pension. Employees must meet the applicable eligibility conditions, and the required contributions and other relevant requirements still matter.

The ruling clarifies that an employer's PF trust rules, by themselves, cannot be used to deny an otherwise eligible employee access to the statutory higher-pension option.

data.title: The week in charts: FPI selloff, Reliance bets, Blinkit's expansion plans
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- From foreign investors continuing to pull money out of Indian equities to unusual leveraged bets on Reliance Industries Ltd, the week saw key developments across markets and business.

Eternal raised its target for Blinkit's dark store expansion, while the government outlined plans to corporatize 11 major ports to speed up decision-making. Meanwhile, Australian pacer Mitchell Starc reached the 450-wicket milestone in men's Test cricket, joining an elite group of bowlers-here is this week's news in numbers.

Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) pulled out Rs.48,056 crore from Indian equities till 23 October, extending the exodus of foreign capital from the market. High crude oil prices, rising US bond yields and a stronger dollar have weighed on investor sentiment.

If October ends with net outflows, it will be the seventh month in 2026 to see foreign investors pull money out of Indian equities. Cumulative net outflows have reached about Rs.3.10 trillion this year, nearly double the Rs.1.66 trillion recorded in 2025.

Last week, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman flagged the flight of foreign capital towards the US and markets offering greater opportunities in artificial intelligence (AI) as 'a concern'.

Two traders have built large leveraged positions in Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL), a move analysts have described as 'rarest of rare', a Mint report said. Stock exchange data shows that both traders hold positions exceeding 3% each of RIL's marketwide position limit (MWPL).

The unusual bets come ahead of the initial public offering (IPO) of Jio Platforms Ltd, RIL's telecom and digital services subsidiary, in which it owns about 66%. They also come as RIL shares have fallen sharply, hitting a 52-week low on 13 October.

India's most-valued listed company, RIL, could see value unlocked through Jio Platforms' public listing, which would give the subsidiary an independent market valuation. However, the rationale behind the traders' bets remains unclear.

Eternal is stepping up its expansion plans for quick-commerce business Blinkit, raising its target to 3,500 dark stores by March 2027 from the earlier target of 3,000. The company had 2,751 stores as of September 2026, adding 308 during the second quarter.

Eternal's consolidated revenue from operations rose 77.6% year-on-year to Rs.24,138 crore in the September quarter. However, profit margins remained thin, and the company reported a cash outflow of Rs.1,813 crore. Blinkit accounted for 80% of Eternal's revenue, making its expansion central to the company's growth plans.

Eternal remains confident that opening more stores in smaller cities will make business sense. The higher store target also comes as its main rival, Zepto, faces hurdles in raising funds.

7.9%: This is the year-on-year growth in India's core sector output in September, up from 5.9% in August. Iron ore, electricity, coal and refinery products led the growth.

759: Number of H-1B visa registrations filed by Infosys for FY27, down from 8,886 a year earlier, amid tighter US immigration policies. TCS registrations fell to 284 from 5,955 last year.

6.5%: Decline in vehicle registrations during this year's Navratri festival, according to the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (Fada). The 2025 festival period had also benefited from GST cuts.

15: Amazon delivery facilities in New York that the e-commerce giant has threatened to close if a proposed bill mandating direct employment of delivery drivers becomes law.

28%: Share of software budgets that large enterprises spend, on average, on vendor upgrades and licensing, leaving less room for investment in AI and innovation, according to a study by software maintenance provider Origina.

The government plans to convert 11 of India's 12 major ports into professionally managed companies with independent boards by 2030. The move aims to speed up decisions on port operations, funding and expansion. Under the current system, administrative processes can slow decisions when cargo patterns change or customers' needs evolve.

Over the past four years, the combined revenue of the 12 major ports has grown at a compounded annual rate of 10.7%. Kamarajar Port near Chennai is the only major port currently run as a company. Under the proposed model, the port company will manage basic infrastructure, while private operators will run terminals and handle cargo under public-private partnership agreements. The new structure is expected to help ports respond more quickly to business needs and facilitate expansion.

Mitchell Starc's 450th Test wicket this week put him among an elite group of 10 bowlers to reach the milestone. The Australian left-arm pacer dismissed South Africa's Wiaan Mulder in the second Test, reaching the landmark in his 109th match. Sri Lankan spinner Muttiah Muralitharan leads the list with 800 wickets in 133 Tests.

However, Starc stands apart for his strike rate, that is, the speed at which he takes wickets. He needs just 46 balls, on average, to claim a wicket-the lowest among the 10 bowlers in the list. That makes him the quickest wicket-taker in the group, though not the most economical. Starc concedes 3.43 runs per over, reflecting the trade-off that comes with his attacking style: he takes wickets quickly but also gives batters more scoring opportunities.
